name: os-taxonomy
one_liner: A free, ready-made map of everything a child learns from preschool through elementary school, broken into thousands of small skills and showing exactly which skills must come before which others.
buyer: A founder building a personalized tutoring app or homeschool curriculum product who would otherwise spend months manually mapping out what to teach in what order.
business_use_cases: An edtech startup uses the prerequisite graph to automatically figure out what a struggling student is actually missing, instead of hand-coding a curriculum sequence.
A homeschool curriculum company builds a personalized weekly lesson planner on top of it, tailored to each child's age and gaps.
A tutoring marketplace uses the standards alignment to automatically match a student's school curriculum to the right practice material.

money_ideas.idea: Build a paid adaptive-practice app on top of the taxonomy that recommends the next skill a child should learn.
Offer a curriculum-mapping service to small tutoring centers or homeschool co-ops using this dataset as the backbone.

steal_this: Build a one-page 'what should my kid learn next' tool this weekend that takes a child's age and one weak subject, and spits out the next five micro-topics to practice.
